story.title: THE QUIET SKY
story.logline: A new pilot joins a tired squadron in France. His first routine patrol reveals enemy scouts watching the roads behind their lines.

briefing.speaker: Captain Edward Mercer

lines.speaker: Captain Edward Mercer
lines.text: Reed, your first patrol. Saint-Martin church, the Scarpe bend, then the mill at Mercatel. Stay this side of the lines.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Thomas Bennett
lines.text: I will be off your right wing. Keep your speed above twenty metres a second. The S.E. will forgive nerves. She will not forgive an empty sky beneath a stalled wing.

lines.speaker: Second Lieutenant Arthur Reed
lines.text: And if the morning is less quiet than promised, sir?

lines.speaker: Captain Edward Mercer
lines.text: Two German scouts were seen over the river yesterday. Drive them off before they can watch the supply road. No lone pursuit across the lines.

lines.speaker: Lieutenant Thomas Bennett
lines.text: Look around as often as you look ahead. And when it is over, bring yourself home. The mess has only just learned your name.

lines.speaker: Second Lieutenant Arthur Reed
lines.text: Three landmarks, one wingman, and home for breakfast. Understood.

text: Fly an airborne patrol from Bertincourt at 400 metres with Bennett in a second S.E.5a.
Follow the marked route through Saint-Martin, the Scarpe bend and Mercatel. Intercept any German scouts that appear at the river.
Clear the patrol and return to the Bertincourt marker. This training sortie ends on the return pass; a landing is not required.

steps.caption: Already airborne north of Bertincourt. Bennett forms on your right wing.
Patrol the church, river bend and mill in order. Keep enough speed to fly.
Two German scouts may cross your route at the river. Clear them together.
When the route and interception are complete, return for a pass over Bertincourt.

intel: Your aircraft: Royal Aircraft Factory S.E.5a, two machine guns, no shields or secondary weapon.
Wingman: Lieutenant Bennett. His survival is an optional objective.
Expected opposition: two Fokker D.VII scouts.
Controls: click to capture the mouse; mouse steers; left click or Space fires; T selects a target; W/S or scroll changes throttle; Z full throttle; Q/E rolls.
Stay above the ground and keep flying speed. Mission starts airborne and finishes at the home marker.

debrief.win: Patrol complete. The scouts have been driven off the supply road and you are back over Bertincourt. First sortie entered in the log.
debrief.lose: The morning patrol did not return safely. Review the route, keep flying speed, and try the sortie again.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Edward Mercer
dialogue.text: You have your first patrol in the book, Reed. Those scouts were looking inland, not toward our trenches. I want to know what drew their attention.

dialogue.speaker: Second Lieutenant Arthur Reed
dialogue.text: The supply road below the river bend. There was a convoy on it.

dialogue.speaker: Captain Edward Mercer
dialogue.text: Then tomorrow we fly over that road before the lorries move. For now, get something warm and write your report.
